A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InvMM research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary Sections 7–10 support reliable comparison, including matching content across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original detection, memorization-factor and membership experiments with DDPM, LDM and Stable Diffusion, plus extensive prompt-inversion experiments in the appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains and revises original empirical results and adds SD v3.5 evaluations and GCG adversarial-prompt case studies.

M1.justification: v3 divides InvMM by latent dimensionality N in Eq. (9) and Algorithm 1, changing the reported score and KL regularizer from total to average KL divergence. The Gaussian inversion, adaptive weighting and Gumbel-Softmax prompt mechanism remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10, CelebAHQ, FFHQ and the confirmed, suspicious and normal LAION subsets for the same memorization, inversion, detection and membership tasks. Discrete and relaxed prompt inversion already appear in v2. SD v3.5 and GCG change model configurations and procedures within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Ren et al. to the SD v1.4 comparison while retaining Wen's detector; the DDPM comparator set is unchanged. v3 also removes the entire explicit AutoPrompt/PEZ comparison from v2 Appendix Section 9.4, substantially reducing comparison coverage of alternative discrete-prompt optimizers.

E3.justification: SD v1.4 detection negatives expand from 50 normal images to 100 suspicious and normal images. v3 Table 1 reports fixed-caption InvMM, corresponding to v2's InvMM* variant. The membership holdout changes from CelebAHQ-250 to 600 images outside FFHQ-6k. SD v3.5 and GCG introduce additional model, optimization and stopping settings. These establish reported protocol changes, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds GCG case studies testing realizable adversarial prompts for suspicious images (Figs. 9b and 13). It removes v2's alternative prompt-optimizer analysis and the per-image replication-frequency study across sampled prompts, noises and guidance scales (Appendix Sections 9.4 and 9.8). Temperature, guidance-scale, objective and adaptive-weight ablations remain.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix Section 8.2 explicitly states that MLOO's ten-fold cross-validation was conducted once. v3 Section 8.3 retains ten-fold cross-validation but removes that repetition-count disclosure. Neither PDF reports confidence intervals, significance tests or across-seed uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Under the expanded negative set, fixed-caption InvMM's Table 1 AUC/TPR@1%FPR changes from 1.000/1.000 to 0.974/0.908; this is not a same-setting performance comparison. Figure 8's infinite-score counts change from 267/372 to 337/372 for CIFAR-10 and from 8/38 to 10/41 for SD v1.4/v2.1, with 74 added for SD v3.5. Membership curves change, GCG and SD v3.5 results are added, and v2's full replication-count results are removed.

T1.justification: Eq. (9) and the Gaussian closed form acquire normalization by N, revising the mathematical measure. Eq. (11) now permits lambda = 0, previously excluded by lambda > 0. The background derivation, entropy argument and Appendix Section 7 variational and reparameterization equations otherwise remain; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v3 drops v2's explicit comparative efficiency claim and foregrounds adversarial completeness and cross-sample commensurability in the abstract and contributions. Much of the worst-case interpretation already appeared in v2 Section 5.3, so the central contribution is refocused rather than replaced.

C2.justification: The introduction now qualifies the generalization concern as heavy or frequent replication. v3 removes v2's blanket conclusion that existing discrete-prompt tuning methods cannot reconstruct training images, and omits the conclusion's proposed online filtering and adversarial-training applications. The Gaussian approximation and relaxed-prompt feasibility limitations remain acknowledged.

D1.justification: v3 documents CLIP-L-only inversion for SD v3.5 with CLIP-G and T5 frozen, plus GCG settings including 20 tokens, 500 steps, batch size 128, top-k 256 and stopping conditions. Implementation and sampling details associated with removed appendix studies disappear. Table 2's default hyperparameters, A800 hardware disclosure and code-access link remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds Jiang et al.'s prompt-free detection work, Ren et al.'s cross-attention method and Zou et al.'s GCG work. AutoPrompt and Hard Prompts Made Easy references disappear with their comparison. Section 2.1 adds a specific distinction from Jiang et al.: InvMM also addresses unconditional diffusion models.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction/contribution narrative and detection discussion are substantially rewritten. Influence-factor experiments move ahead of detection, exchanging Sections 5.3 and 5.4. The supplement gains an overview and reorganized subsections, alongside notation and wording corrections, corresponding-author information and acknowledgements.

P2.justification: Empirical plots are extensively repacked and their InvMM axes rescaled. v2 Figure 6 is split between v3 Figures 6 and 11. Table 1 changes row structure; GCG panels and SD v3.5 image grids are added; AutoPrompt/PEZ and full replication-check displays are removed. Many remaining appendix figures are retained with changed numbering or placement.

improvement.justification: The selected GCG examples partially close v2's gap between relaxed-prompt inversion and realizable attacks. Adding suspicious negatives and the Ren baseline also makes the caption-based detection comparison more informative. These gains are limited by removal of the AutoPrompt/PEZ comparison and full replication-frequency evidence, while the Gaussian and soft-prompt limitations remain. The revision improves practical validation modestly, without establishing same-setting performance gains.
